summary: Iteration-6 (REAL per-service Graph migration via graph_migrations.DISPATCH + stats persistence on job doc) backend testing complete. Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6.py with 20 pytest cases covering: (1) DISPATCH module correctness — 9 keys matching the 9 service_types, all async functions, each with (item, src, dst, _graph_request) signature; (2) graph_adapter.migrate_item return shape — simulated (no creds) returns {status, error, duration_ms, stats:{}} with success/failed status and int duration; live w/ bad creds returns {status:'failed', error:<MSAL authority error msg>, duration_ms, stats:{}}; unknown service_type also returns failed dict with stats={}; (3) public_folders unsupported message contains 'Public Folders' + (MRS or 3rd-party or PowerShell) guidance; (4) simulated regression — 5-item exchange job runs to completion (status='completed', progress=100, success+fail=5), and CRITICALLY every item has the new 'stats' dict field (may be {}); (5) all 9 service_types are discoverable in simulated mode and job creation queues successfully for each (parametrized); (6) live-mode dispatch pre-flight — project with fake structurally-valid creds → POST /api/jobs returns HTTP 400 with detail starting 'Graph discovery failed:' (NOT 500); (7) stats persistence via in-process _process_item — monkeypatched graph_adapter.migrate_item returns {stats:{messages_copied:5, bytes:1024, folders_copied:2}}; after direct in-process call to server._process_item, db.jobs doc has items.0.stats == returned dict AND aggregate_stats.messages_copied=5, aggregate_stats.bytes=1024, aggregate_stats.folders_copied=2, plus completed_count=1, success_count=1, progress=100; and (8) empty stats={} (simulated mode) does NOT create/populate aggregate_stats — verified aggregate_stats is either missing or {}. Regression: 106/106 (86 prior + 20 iter6). Fixed 1 iter5 assertion that expected status in (200,500) for legacy-plaintext discover — iter6 changed the error path to a clean HTTPException(400) 'Graph discovery failed:' (this is the exact improvement the iter5 report flagged as a minor issue). Updated test_iteration5.py to also accept 400, preserving the intent (verify decrypt-related errors are NOT the cause).
critical_code_review_comments: graph_migrations.py:370-380 & 581-604 — _copy_file / _copy_site_file call `from graph_adapter import acquire_token` inside the function AND bypass the tenacity-wrapped _graph_request for direct httpx.put on {put_url or upload_url}. The upload session PUT is fine (uploadUrl is anonymous / pre-authorized), but the SMALL-FILE PUT to /users/{id}/drive/root:/{path}:/content uses `token = await acquire_token(dst)` and issues a raw httpx.put with NO retry/backoff. A 429/503 during a large migration will fail permanently for that file. Recommend either routing the small-file PUT through _graph_request (adding a `content=` param) or wrapping it in the same tenacity retry.

graph_migrations.py:64-94 — _find_or_provision_dest_user auto-provisions users in the destination with a base64-derived 12-char password + '9x' suffix. This will bypass conditional access / password policies in many tenants and hardcodes the temporary password into logs if the POST body is ever traced. Consider (a) surfacing a `provision_users=false` flag on the project, (b) generating with `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`, (c) sending the temp password to the notifier instead of storing/logging.

graph_migrations.py:363-380 & 576-589 — _copy_file downloads the ENTIRE file into memory (`r.content`) even for large files (>4MB), then re-slices for chunked upload. A 5 GB OneDrive file will OOM the pod. Recommend streaming: `client.stream('GET', dl_url)` + iterate chunks + upload each range as it arrives.

graph_migrations.py:130-147 — mail folder creation `try/except: pass` swallows all errors and only recovers by re-listing by displayName. This silently drops folders that fail with non-'already exists' errors (e.g. permission, quota). Recommend catching only 409 conflict, letting other errors propagate.

graph_migrations.py:611-676 — migrate_team converts a group→team via PUT /groups/{id}/team AFTER group creation, which is Graph-supported but the group provisioning is async: sleep(3) then PUT will race in tenants with slow group provisioning. Consider polling GET /groups/{id} until the group has a provisioningStatus, or catching a specific 404/409 and retrying with backoff.

graph_adapter.py:305-335 (migrate_item live path) — result.setdefault('stats', {}) is defensive but doesn't validate that stats values are numeric before server._process_item runs $inc on them. If a per-service fn ever returns stats={'note': 'string'}, the isinstance filter at server.py:475 will skip it (safe), but a stats value that's a dict/list would still be preserved on items.$.stats. Consider validating stats shape (all values int|float) in graph_adapter itself.

server.py:459-477 (_process_item stats persistence) — the $set items.$.stats and $inc aggregate_stats.<k> use two separate update_one calls. Between them, a concurrent read (e.g. GET /jobs/{id}) can see items[0].stats populated but aggregate_stats not yet incremented. For a live job with high concurrency this creates transient inconsistency. Recommend combining both mutations into a single update_one with both $set and $inc.

graph_migrations.py:213-215 & 251-253 — several fns catch and log with `logger.warning(...)` then `continue`, silently accumulating no-op success. The final result is still {'status': 'success'} even if 100% of children failed. Recommend tracking failure_count in stats and returning 'partial' when failure_count > 0 (like migrate_sharepoint_site already does).

graph_migrations.py:353-358 — 'no download URL for item' RuntimeError is raised but not caught up-slope in _copy_drive_children (line 346 catches Exception). It'll be logged as a warning and swallowed. Since this is an unrecoverable failure for that file, it should increment a stats.files_failed counter.
